# Metric Sector Catalog (generated)

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate_metric_sector_catalog.py from data/malachite/*.textproto and
     data/metric_baseline_semantics.json. Do not edit by hand; regenerate. -->

This file supplies every metric-specific slot in the generic templates
(`templates/pipelines/dual_sector_fusion_3stage.yl2`, `multi_sector_fusion_4stage.yl2`,
`rollup_sector_fusion_4stage.yl2`, `rollup_sector_fusion_5stage.yl2`, and the event filter / observed
value / entity field slots of the other pipelines). Source of truth:
the compiler's own `config.textproto` (valid dimension sets) and `dimension_field_mapping.textproto`
(dimension → UDM fields), plus our restatement of each metric's baseline SQL.

## How to use a row

* **Observed event filter**: paste every line into the stage's event section, one per line. These
  lines select the same events the 30-day baseline counts, so observed and baseline are comparable.
  Do not substitute a `metadata.event_type` guess; several baselines (DNS, HTTP, network, alerts,
  workspace) do not filter on event type at all.
* **Observed value**: the stage outcome expression for today's value (`$obs = <value>`).
* **Metric arg**: the `metric:` argument of the `metrics.<name>(...)` call.
* **Entity identifier fields**: fields that may appear *alone* as the metric's filter (one valid
  single-dimension set). Bind the same field in the event section (`<field> = $entity`) and in the
  metric call (`<field>: $entity`). Defaults: `userid` for users, `hostname` for devices.
* **Composite-only** metrics have no single-field set. Every call must supply one complete valid
  dimension set (listed in the row). They become fusion sectors only as a **roll-up sector** (below).
* **Roll-up sector sets** (composite-only rows): each block is one valid set with exactly one entity
  dimension. Fill `rollup_sector_fusion_4stage.yl2` / `_5stage.yl2` sector A from it: the detail stage
  binds the entity plus every companion (*Detail bindings*), matches on *Match keys*, and passes
  *Metric filters* to every `metrics.<name>(...)` call; the roll-up stage counts distinct *Distinct key*.

## The exact-set rule (compiler)

The compiler maps every filter argument of a `metrics.*()` call to its dimension and requires the
resulting *set* to equal one valid set exactly (`ueba_validator.go`). Adding a field that is valid
elsewhere still fails if the combined set is not listed. Example: `auth_attempts_fail` accepts
`principal.asset.hostname` + `target.user.userid` but rejects `principal.asset.hostname` +
`target.asset.hostname`.

## Fusion pairing rules (`dual_sector_fusion_3stage`, `multi_sector_fusion_4stage`, `rollup_sector_fusion_*`)

1. Same entity kind on both sides: user ↔ user or device ↔ device. Never user ↔ host.
2. Same identifier on both sides: userid ↔ userid, hostname ↔ hostname, email_addresses ↔
   email_addresses. Principal vs. target does not matter (`target.user.userid` joins
   `principal.user.userid`).
3. Each sector's entity field must be listed below for its metric.
4. A composite-only metric (e.g. `file_executions_*`, so process execution + DNS) can be a sector only as a
   roll-up sector in `rollup_sector_fusion_4stage.yl2` (or `_5stage.yl2` with fleet normalization), and at
   most one sector per query may be a roll-up. Its Z is the largest per-key Z for the entity (per binary,
   product or rule), not a Z of the entity's total volume: no entity-only baseline exists. Add an
   `// ADVISORY:` line saying so. Its entity must be the only entity dimension of one listed roll-up set.
5. Two metrics of the same family (e.g. `auth_attempts_fail` + `auth_attempts_total`) are allowed but
   correlated; add an `// ADVISORY:` line to the query header saying so.
6. `email_addresses`, `ip` and `mac` are repeated fields: one event can fan out to several entities.

### `metrics.alert_event_name_count`

* **Family**: alert
* **Baseline counts**: log_type in (CB_EDR, CS_EDR, MICROSOFT_GRAPH_ALERT, SENTINELONE_ALERTS); no event_type filter
* **Observed event filter**:
  ```yara
  (metadata.log_type = "CB_EDR" or metadata.log_type = "CS_EDR" or metadata.log_type = "MICROSOFT_GRAPH_ALERT" or metadata.log_type = "SENTINELONE_ALERTS")
  ```
* **Observed value**: `count(metadata.id)`
* **Metric arg**: `metric: event_count_sum`
* **Composite-only**: yes. Every call needs one complete valid set:
  * PRINCIPAL_DEVICE + SECURITY_RESULT_RULE_NAME
  * PRINCIPAL_DEVICE + PRINCIPAL_PROCESS_FILE_PATH + SECURITY_RESULT_RULE_NAME
  * PRINCIPAL_DEVICE + PRINCIPAL_PROCESS_FILE_PATH + PRINCIPAL_USER + SECURITY_RESULT_RULE_NAME
  * PRINCIPAL_DEVICE + PRINCIPAL_PROCESS_FILE_HASH + PRINCIPAL_USER + SECURITY_RESULT_RULE_NAME
* **Roll-up sector sets** (sector A of `rollup_sector_fusion_*`; smallest set per entity dimension. Any other set above with exactly one user/device dimension works the same way: bind every other dimension):
  * **PRINCIPAL_DEVICE** (device) + SECURITY_RESULT_RULE_NAME
    * Entity field: any PRINCIPAL_DEVICE field (see *Dimension → UDM fields*); default `principal.asset.hostname`
    * Detail bindings: `security_result.rule_name = $security_result_rule_name`; `$security_result_rule_name != ""`
    * Match keys: `$entity, $security_result_rule_name`
    * Metric filters: `<entity field>: $entity, security_result.rule_name: $security_result_rule_name`
    * Distinct key: `security_result_rule_name`

* **Note**: HTTP_PRESENT approximation, verified against baselines for MUGATU and 172.16.2.6 (see provenance). A method-only filter misses user-agent-only events; an event_type-only filter overcounts Zeek NETWORK_HTTP rows with no http fields.

### `metrics.network_bytes_total`

  * PRINCIPAL_USER (user): `principal.user.product_object_id`, `principal.user.email_addresses`, `principal.user.userid`, `principal.user.windows_sid`, `principal.user.employee_id`
* **Other valid dimension sets**: PRINCIPAL_COUNTRY + PRINCIPAL_DEVICE; PRINCIPAL_COUNTRY + PRINCIPAL_USER; PRINCIPAL_DEVICE + SECURITY_CATEGORY; PRINCIPAL_USER + SECURITY_CATEGORY; PRINCIPAL_DEVICE + TARGET_NETWORK_ORGANIZATION_NAME; PRINCIPAL_USER + TARGET_NETWORK_ORGANIZATION_NAME; PRINCIPAL_DEVICE + TARGET_DEVICE; PRINCIPAL_USER + TARGET_DEVICE

### `metrics.resource_creation_fail`

* **Family**: cloud_resource
* **Baseline counts**: event_type in (RESOURCE_CREATION, USER_RESOURCE_CREATION) and not (UNKNOWN_ACTION or ALLOW in actions)
* **Observed event filter**:
  ```yara
  (metadata.event_type = "RESOURCE_CREATION" or metadata.event_type = "USER_RESOURCE_CREATION")
  not security_result.action = "ALLOW"
  ```
* **Observed value**: `count(metadata.id)`
* **Metric arg**: `metric: event_count_sum`
* **Composite-only**: yes. Every call needs one complete valid set:
  * PRODUCT_NAME + TARGET_USER + VENDOR_NAME
  * PRINCIPAL_USER + PRODUCT_NAME + VENDOR_NAME
  * PRINCIPAL_IP + PRINCIPAL_USER + PRODUCT_NAME + VENDOR_NAME
  * PRINCIPAL_USER + PRODUCT_NAME + TARGET_APPLICATION + VENDOR_NAME
  * PRINCIPAL_USER + PRODUCT_NAME + TARGET_RESOURCE_NAME + VENDOR_NAME
  * PRINCIPAL_USER + PRODUCT_NAME + TARGET_RESOURCE_NAME + TARGET_RESOURCE_TYPE + VENDOR_NAME
  * PRINCIPAL_USER + PRODUCT_NAME + TARGET_APPLICATION + TARGET_LOCATION_NAME + VENDOR_NAME
* **Roll-up sector sets** (sector A of `rollup_sector_fusion_*`; smallest set per entity dimension. Any other set above with exactly one user/device dimension works the same way: bind every other dimension):
  * **PRINCIPAL_USER** (user) + PRODUCT_NAME + VENDOR_NAME
    * Entity field: any PRINCIPAL_USER field (see *Dimension → UDM fields*); default `principal.user.userid`
    * Detail bindings: `metadata.product_name = $product_name`; `$product_name != ""`; `metadata.vendor_name = $vendor_name`; `$vendor_name != ""`
    * Match keys: `$entity, $product_name, $vendor_name`
    * Metric filters: `<entity field>: $entity, metadata.product_name: $product_name, metadata.vendor_name: $vendor_name`
    * Distinct key: `product_name`
  * **TARGET_USER** (user) + PRODUCT_NAME + VENDOR_NAME
    * Entity field: any TARGET_USER field (see *Dimension → UDM fields*); default `target.user.userid`
    * Detail bindings: `metadata.product_name = $product_name`; `$product_name != ""`; `metadata.vendor_name = $vendor_name`; `$vendor_name != ""`
    * Match keys: `$entity, $product_name, $vendor_name`
    * Metric filters: `<entity field>: $entity, metadata.product_name: $product_name, metadata.vendor_name: $vendor_name`
    * Distinct key: `product_name`

## Sibling triads (`part_of_the_whole_triad_multilevel.yl2`)

One stage (`all_entities`) observes three sibling metrics for the same entity, then compares each
against the personal 30-day baseline, the team cohort and the enterprise. Because one stage carries
all three metrics:

1. **One entity field for all three.** It must be valid alone for every metric (listed per triad).
   Bind it once: `<entity field> = $user` (or `$host`) in the stage and `<entity field>: $user` in all
   six `metrics.*()` calls.
2. **Stage filter = the union, not any one metric's filter.** Paste the triad's *Stage event filter*
   lines into the `event_filter` slot. Never add one metric's own extra line (e.g.
   `security_result.action = "ALLOW"`) to the stage: it zeroes the sibling counts.
3. **Observed values.** Use the triad's *Observed values*: counts whose metric adds a filter line are
   conditional sums over that line, so each observed value counts the same events as its baseline.
   Fail + success = total (verified live: Administrator 6241 = 6171 fail + 70 success; DNS on
   mikeross-pc 4 = 3 + 1). Outbound and inbound overlap: a flow with both sent and received bytes counts
   in both, so outbound + inbound can exceed total.
4. **Only the triads below.** Composite-only families (`file_executions_*`, `resource_*`,
   `alert_event_name_count`) cannot form a triad: the stage matches the entity alone and those metrics
   have no entity-only baseline. For process execution use a per-(host, hash) pipeline or a roll-up
   sector. Do not mix families into a triad (e.g. `dns_bytes_outbound` with DNS query counts: it counts
   port-53 traffic, not DNS messages); use a sector fusion instead.
5. **Math (as the template computes it).** Per metric: $Z_{personal}$, $Z_{vs\_team}$,
   $Z_{vs\_enterprise}$. Composite: $D_{vs\_team}^2 = \sum_{m=1}^{3} Z_{vs\_team,m}^2$. The terms are
   **two-sided**, so a collapse (e.g. success drops while fail rises) also raises $D$. To score surges
   only, rectify each term in the root outcome: `$z1_sq = if($z1_vs_team > 0, $z1_vs_team * $z1_vs_team, 0)`.
6. Byte triads observe `sum(network.sent_bytes)` / `sum(network.received_bytes)` over the union of
   rows; the per-metric `< 1000000000000000` guard is not applied per metric, so a single corrupt
   row (>= 1e15 bytes) can inflate one observed value.

### Auth triad

* **Metrics (m1, m2, m3)**: `auth_attempts_total`, `auth_attempts_fail`, `auth_attempts_success`
* **Entity dimensions valid for all three**: PRINCIPAL_DEVICE (device, default `principal.asset.hostname`); PRINCIPAL_USER (user, default `principal.user.userid`); TARGET_USER (user, default `target.user.userid`). Any field of the chosen dimension works (see *Dimension → UDM fields*).
* **Stage event filter** (`event_filter` slot):
  ```yara
  metadata.event_type = "USER_LOGIN"
  ```
* **Observed values**:
  * `m1_observation_agg` (auth_attempts_total): `count(metadata.id)`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`
  * `m2_observation_agg` (auth_attempts_fail): `sum(if(security_result.action = "ALLOW", 0, 1))`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`
  * `m3_observation_agg` (auth_attempts_success): `sum(if(security_result.action = "ALLOW", 1, 0))`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`

### DNS triad

* **Metrics (m1, m2, m3)**: `dns_queries_total`, `dns_queries_fail`, `dns_queries_success`
* **Entity dimensions valid for all three**: PRINCIPAL_DEVICE (device, default `principal.asset.hostname`); PRINCIPAL_USER (user, default `principal.user.userid`). Any field of the chosen dimension works (see *Dimension → UDM fields*).
* **Stage event filter** (`event_filter` slot):
  ```yara
  (network.dns.questions.name != "" or network.dns.answers.name != "" or network.dns.id != 0)
  ```
* **Observed values**:
  * `m1_observation_agg` (dns_queries_total): `count(metadata.id)`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`
  * `m2_observation_agg` (dns_queries_fail): `sum(if(network.dns.response_code != 0, 1, 0))`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`
  * `m3_observation_agg` (dns_queries_success): `sum(if(network.dns.response_code = 0, 1, 0))`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`

### HTTP triad

* **Metrics (m1, m2, m3)**: `http_queries_total`, `http_queries_fail`, `http_queries_success`
* **Entity dimensions valid for all three**: PRINCIPAL_DEVICE (device, default `principal.asset.hostname`); PRINCIPAL_USER (user, default `principal.user.userid`). Any field of the chosen dimension works (see *Dimension → UDM fields*).
* **Stage event filter** (`event_filter` slot):
  ```yara
  (network.http.method != "" or network.http.user_agent != "" or network.http.response_code != 0 or network.http.referral_url != "")
  ```
* **Observed values**:
  * `m1_observation_agg` (http_queries_total): `count(metadata.id)`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`
  * `m2_observation_agg` (http_queries_fail): `sum(if(network.http.response_code >= 400, 1, 0))`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`
  * `m3_observation_agg` (http_queries_success): `sum(if(network.http.response_code < 400, 1, 0))`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`

### Network bytes triad

* **Metrics (m1, m2, m3)**: `network_bytes_total`, `network_bytes_outbound`, `network_bytes_inbound`
* **Entity dimensions valid for all three**: PRINCIPAL_DEVICE (device, default `principal.asset.hostname`); PRINCIPAL_USER (user, default `principal.user.userid`). Any field of the chosen dimension works (see *Dimension → UDM fields*).
* **Stage event filter** (`event_filter` slot):
  ```yara
  ((network.sent_bytes > 0 and network.sent_bytes < 1000000000000000) or (network.received_bytes > 0 and network.received_bytes < 1000000000000000))
  ```
* **Observed values**:
  * `m1_observation_agg` (network_bytes_total): `sum(network.sent_bytes) + sum(network.received_bytes)`; metric arg `metric: value_sum`
  * `m2_observation_agg` (network_bytes_outbound): `sum(network.sent_bytes)`; metric arg `metric: value_sum`
  * `m3_observation_agg` (network_bytes_inbound): `sum(network.received_bytes)`; metric arg `metric: value_sum`

### Network flows triad

* **Metrics (m1, m2, m3)**: `network_flows_total`, `network_flows_outbound`, `network_flows_inbound`
* **Entity dimensions valid for all three**: PRINCIPAL_DEVICE (device, default `principal.asset.hostname`); PRINCIPAL_USER (user, default `principal.user.userid`). Any field of the chosen dimension works (see *Dimension → UDM fields*).
* **Stage event filter** (`event_filter` slot):
  ```yara
  ((network.sent_bytes > 0 and network.sent_bytes < 1000000000000000) or (network.received_bytes > 0 and network.received_bytes < 1000000000000000))
  ```
* **Observed values**:
  * `m1_observation_agg` (network_flows_total): `count(metadata.id)`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`
  * `m2_observation_agg` (network_flows_outbound): `sum(if(network.sent_bytes > 0 and network.sent_bytes < 1000000000000000, 1, 0))`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`
  * `m3_observation_agg` (network_flows_inbound): `sum(if(network.received_bytes > 0 and network.received_bytes < 1000000000000000, 1, 0))`; metric arg `metric: event_count_sum`

## Dimension → UDM fields

| Dimension | UDM fields |
| :--- | :--- |
| CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_HASH | `network.tls.client.certificate.sha256` |
| DNS_DOMAIN | `network.dns_domain` |
| DNS_QUERY_TYPE | `network.dns.questions.type` |
| EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS | `network.email.from` |
| EMAIL_TO_ADDRESS | `network.email.to` |
| EVENT_TYPE | `metadata.event_type` |
| HTTP_USER_AGENT | `network.http.user_agent` |
| MAIL_ID | `network.email.mail_id` |
